sections.content:
Population change in Cornwall in 2032

The population in Cornwall is projected to increase from 575,532 people in 2022 to 626,317 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net internal migration, which will increase the population by 74,338 people.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Cornwall
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Cornwall, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More deaths than births mean that the population is projected to decrease by 25,674, with 45,329 births and 71,003 deaths in Cornwall between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would decrease the population in Cornwall by 4.5%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to increase the population by 74,338, with 279,199 people moving to the area and 204,860 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Cornwall by 12.9%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 2,730, with 14,943 people moving to the area and 17,673 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Cornwall by 0.5%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 4,981, with 23,352 people moving to the area and 18,371 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Cornwall by 0.9%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Cornwall in 2032

The median age in Cornwall is projected to rise from 47 years in 2022 to 49 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 27% of the population in Cornwall are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 24% in 2022.

sections.title: The 80 to 89 age group are set to see the largest change in Cornwall between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Cornwall is projected to stay the same, at around 59%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 406 to 429 over the same time period.

This is above average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Cornwall?

In 2032, 17% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 19% in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Cornwall between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will stay around the same, at 4%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 7% to 6%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
